species: Drosophila melanogaster (native head membranes; nAChR population not resolved to subunits)
source: Tomizawa, Latli and Casida 1996, J Neurochem 67(4):1669-1676, doi:10.1046/j.1471-4159.1996.67041669.x, PMID 8858952 ("Head membranes of Drosophila melanogaster and Musca domestica have a single high-affinity binding site for [3H]IMI with KD values of 1-2 nM and Bmax values of 560-850 fmol/mg of protein"). This is a radioligand saturation Kd measured on the MODELLED organism, which is why it is the library's only binding_occupancy row. Two honest limits are recorded rather than smoothed over: (a) the publication states the 1-2 nM range for Drosophila and Musca jointly and does not resolve the Drosophila-only value, so FlyLab takes the conservative (weakest-affinity) end, 2.0e-9 M, and the tier stays literature_order; (b) the preparation is native head membranes and resolves NO subunit - the companion photoaffinity study (Tomizawa and Casida 1997, Neurosci Lett 237:61, PMID 9453215, doi:10.1016/s0304-3940(97)00811-2) labels a single 66 kDa ligand-binding polypeptide of the Drosophila nAChR without assigning it to a named Dalpha/Dbeta subunit - so the row sits on the preparation-resolved key insect_nAChR_native_dmel and makes no subunit claim. It does not replace the Dederer hybrid-receptor EC50 on the aggregate insect_nAChR key, which is a functional potency and stays where it was.

FlyLab uses the high-affinity Kd = 8.3e-11 M. This is a genuine equilibrium dissociation constant from a radioligand binding assay, but it was measured in an APHID, not in Drosophila. Under the v0.6.1 rule a binding constant licenses physical binding_occupancy only with relation exact_compound_exact_receptor_exact_species, so this row sits at evidence distance E1 and drives binding_engagement_proxy: the same Hill number, reported as an engagement proxy derived from a binding constant measured in another species, and carrying a provenance warning that names the gap. The transfer of an aphid beta1 affinity to the Drosophila Dbeta1 receptor is an assumption, not a measurement.
